summary: Return the minimum number of rooms needed so that no two overlapping meetings share a room.
mainInsight: Process meetings by start time and keep a min-heap of end times of rooms in use. If the earliest-ending room is free by the new start, reuse it (pop); then push the new end. The heap size is the number of rooms.
invariant: After processing meeting i, the heap holds one end time per room opened so far, and its minimum is the room that frees up first.
canonicalApproach: Sort by start + min-heap of end times

approaches.name: Sort by start + min-heap of end times
approaches.summary: Reuse the earliest-ending room when it is free.

approaches.name: Two sorted arrays (sweep)
approaches.summary: Sort starts and ends separately; walk starts, freeing a room when the next end <= start.

approaches.name: Difference array / events
approaches.summary: +1 at each start, -1 at each end, take the max prefix sum.
approaches.timeComplexity: O(n log n) or O(n + T)

commonMistakes: Sorting by end time instead of start time.
Using < instead of <=, so a meeting starting when another ends gets a new room.
Processing start before end on equal times in the event sweep.
edgeCases: One long meeting covering all others.

promptVariants: Why compare the new meeting with the minimum end time in the heap?
Which room should a new meeting try to reuse?
options: The earliest-ending room is free first; if it is busy, all are
The room with the latest end has the most free time
The heap minimum is the shortest meeting so far
Any room works, the minimum is just the cheapest to read
cards.answer: The earliest-ending room is free first; if it is busy, all are
cards.explanation: If even the room that frees up first is still busy at this start, every room is busy and a new one is needed.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The room with the latest end has the mos: The latest-ending room is the last to free up.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The heap minimum is the shortest meeting: The heap holds end times, not durations.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Any room works, the minimum is just the: A room is only reusable if it has ended; the minimum is the only candidate that might have.

promptVariants: One long meeting [1,10] and three back-to-back short ones. How many rooms?
cards.explanation: The long meeting holds one room. The short meetings touch end to start, so they reuse a second room in turn.

incorrectOptionExplanations.4: The short meetings never overlap each other (they only touch).
incorrectOptionExplanations.3: That would be true only if touching meetings conflicted.

promptVariants: What does using < instead of <= get wrong?
options: A room whose meeting ends at t is free at t
It makes the heap pop the wrong element
It prevents the heap from ever being empty
It changes the sort order of the intervals
cards.answer: A room whose meeting ends at t is free at t
cards.explanation: Touching meetings do not overlap, so the room can be reused; < would open an extra room for each back-to-back pair.

incorrectOptionExplanations.It makes the heap pop the wrong element: heappop always removes the minimum; the issue is whether to pop.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It prevents the heap from ever being emp: The heap is non-empty after the first push either way.
incorrectOptionExplanations.It changes the sort order of the interva: Sorting happens before and is unaffected.

promptVariants: How do you solve this without a heap?
cards.answer: Sort all starts and all ends separately. Walk the starts with pointer i and keep pointer j on the ends. For each start, if ends[j] <= start, a room was freed: j += 1 (reuse). Otherwise rooms += 1. The answer is the rooms count. Same O(n log n), and it only counts rooms instead of tracking them.
keyPoints: Advance end pointer when ends[j] <= start
cards.explanation: Which meeting ends does not matter, only how many have ended, which is why the arrays can be sorted independently.

promptVariants: What is the time complexity of the canonical code?
Derive the running time of sort + heap.
cards.explanation: Sorting is O(n log n) and each meeting does at most one pop and one push, O(log n) each.

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(n): Both the sort and the heap add log factors.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O(n * k), k rooms: That is scanning all rooms per meeting instead of using the heap minimum.
